## 41. Samba passwords were not set in a new share container — `QSD5.244` (2026-10-08)
Found by the QualityCheck test `snapshots_2nodes` (step "Create some CIFS and copy one file using usr1"), on `QSD5.243`: right after the share was created `smbclient -U usr1%<password>` answered `NT_STATUS_LOGON_FAILURE` and `pdbedit -L` in the share container listed no user. `cifs.py` (new share) and `UnixAddUser` (new user) set the samba password with `docker exec <CIFS-ip> /hostetc/smbuserfix.sh x <user> <password>`, i.e. with the script `/etc/smbuserfix.sh` of the node, but only `UnixAddUser_sync` (the non-leader path) copies `/TopStor/smbuserfix.sh` there; the leader creates the users through `UnixAddUser` and never ran it, so the file did not exist on a freshly reset node (`/hostetc/smbuserfix.sh: not found`, errors swallowed). `cifs.py` and `UnixAddUser` now copy the script before they use it. Shared code, both flavours. Verified: three users in `pdbedit`, usr1 (group grp1) writes into the share, usr2/usr3 (grp2) get `NT_STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED`. `QSD5.245`: the password step also ran too early on a share container started by a take-over (`docker run -d` returns before samba answers, `cifs.sh` sleeps 1 s, the swallowed error left the share without users, `NT_STATUS_LOGON_FAILURE` after the fail-over); `cifs.py` now repeats the step for each user until `pdbedit -L -u <user>` lists it (up to ~40 s). Verified: after the stop of the owner node the share restarted on the other node with all three users and usr1 could write at once.

## 42. Cron never ran in the container flavour (periodic snapshots) — `QSD5.245` (2026-10-08)

## 43. A volume larger than its pool is accepted on purpose — `QSD5.247` (2026-10-08)
`QSD5.246` refused a CIFS/NFS/HOME/iSCSI volume whose size was larger than the pool's available space (the QualityCheck test `cifs_2nodes`, step "Create a CIFS Volume with Size > Pool", had failed on the old behaviour). The maintainer decided the opposite: **a quota larger than the free space must be accepted** (thin provisioning: a CIFS/NFS/HOME size is a quota, not a reservation). `QSD5.247` removes that check again (`fapi.py` `volumecreate`, message `Volsz1`), so a quota is accepted whatever the free space is. An iSCSI volume is a zvol that reserves its size and still fails on the node when it does not fit (message `ISCSI1006`). Shared code, both flavours.

## 44. Open items closed — `QSD5.247` (2026-10-08)
Findings of the QualityCheck tests of 2026-10-08 that had been left open:
- **Node Config privilege was not enforced (both flavours).** The privilege `Error` ("Node Config" in `usersauth`) was only a hint for the UI; `hosts/config` and `hosts/joincluster` accepted any logged-in user. `fapi.py` has `has_privilege()` (same rule as `privthis.sh`: `admin`/`system` always, others need the privilege) and both endpoints refuse without it: answer `error: noprivilege` (`joinstatus: noprivilege` for the join), message `Priv1004`.
- **Create without a pool answered HTTP 500 (both flavours).** `volumecreate` looked the pool up unchecked (`KeyError`). It now answers `error: nopool` with the message `Volpool1`, nothing is run.
- **iSCSI used the NFS messages (both flavours).** `VolumeCreateISCSI`/`VolumeDeleteISCSI` now log `ISCSI1004/1006/1007` and `ISCSI1000/1001/1002` ("... iSCSI volume ...") instead of `NFS100x`.
- **Not changed, by design:** `showmount` does not work against the NFS containers - they are NFSv4-only (only port 2049 is published, `rpc.mountd --no-nfs-version 2/3`), NFSv4 needs no mount protocol; the client mounts `server:/`. 

## 45. Domain CIFS volumes: DNS name of the AD server and the `_1` test — `QSD5.248` (2026-10-08)
Found by the QualityCheck test `cifs_domain_2nodes` (steps "Create a CIFS Volume for Domain ... using the active directory server name", "CIF volume with 10.11.11.232 ip in the Domain"), with a Samba AD domain controller as the domain:
- **`resolve_dns.sh` asked the wrong DNS server first (both flavours).** The API resolves `domsrv` (the AD server's name) with `resolve_dns.sh`, which adds the cluster's DNS server (`dnsname/<host>`, set with `hosts/config dnsname=... dnssearch=...`) to `resolv.conf`. It wrote it as the SECOND line, behind the resolver the `flask` container already has (docker's `10.11.12.7`), which answers NXDOMAIN for the domain; the resolver stops there, so the creation always ended with `CIFS1033` (name not resolved). The cluster DNS server is now written first.
- **A domain/NFS/HOME volume whose name contains `_1` was never activated (both flavours).** `VolumeActivateCIFSdom`, `VolumeActivateHome`, `VolumeActivateNFS` detect "no volumes" with `grep "\\_1"` on the answer of `etcdget`; volume names are `<name>_<random number>`, so a name like `dom10_181121547` matched too, the script answered "No Volumes _1" and exited: the volume was created (dataset, etcd entry, message "Success creating volume") but its share container never started (about one volume in ten, the same family of bug as `VolumeCreateHOME` in §35). The test now accepts only the not-found marker by itself.

## 46. A FAULTED mirror disk was never replaced in the container flavour — `QSD5.249` (2026-10-08)

## 47. Service Performance page: heartbeat 500, no Prometheus route, Grafana link — `QSD5.250` (2026-10-08)
Found by the QualityCheck test `performance_metrics`, driven with a real headless browser (Chromium + Playwright) against `https://<cluster>/#/performance`:
- **`POST /api/v1/telemetry/heartbeat` answered 500 `name 'time' is not defined` (both flavours).** The start-up clock import in `fapi.py` was changed to `import time as _startclock` and the plain `import time` that `telemetry_heartbeat()` uses was lost. The page pings it every 3 s ("boost mode"), so the browser console filled with 500 errors and the telemetry boost never ran. `import time` is back.
- **No `/prometheus` route in the web server (both flavours).** The page asks `GET /prometheus/api/v1/query`; `httpd_template.conf` proxied only `/api` and `/netdata`, so the request was answered by the UI's index page: every Prometheus number was 0 (ARC, throughput, CPU, latency) and the charts stayed empty. Both web vhosts (443 and 81) now have `ProxyPass /prometheus/ http://<cluster>:9090/` (with the trailing slashes on both sides: without them Apache sends `//api/...` and Prometheus answers a 307 redirect). Verified: the six queries of the page return data, the charts move (peak load / average change from 0.0 to 23 / 18 %), no console errors.
- **"Launch Grafana" opened `http://<cluster>:4000` but Grafana serves HTTPS only (UI).** A plain-HTTP request got HTTP 400. The link is now `https://<host>:4000` (`topstorweb/src/QServicePerformance.jsx`, UI rebuilt); it opens the Grafana login (13.2.3).
Observed, not changed: the page polls Prometheus every 0.25 s while the heartbeat keeps the boost alive (about 30 requests/s from one open page, by design), and the summary cards (users, pools, volumes) are read once when the page is opened.

## 48. Replication between two clusters in the container flavour — `QSD5.251` (2026-10-08)
Found by the QualityCheck test `replication_1node_2transmitter-1recv` (steps "add a Sender / Receiver partner", "users and groups are replicating"), cluster 1 (one node) -> cluster 2 (two nodes):
- **The replication port was never opened (container flavour).** `receivekeys.sh` (run on the partner cluster by the key exchange) writes `Port <repliport>` into `sshd_config` and calls `systemctl restart sshd`; in a node container the `systemctl` wrapper does not restart sshd, so the port (2400 in the test) was never listened on and the sender got `Connection refused` for ever (`activatetunnels.sh`: "still closed"). `receivekeys.sh` now sends SIGHUP to sshd (`pkill -HUP -x sshd`, only when `is_container`), which re-reads the configuration and listens on the new port.
- **The tunnels to the partner's other nodes never started (both flavours).** The tunnel scripts are generated from `LREMOTE.sh` / `RREMOTE.sh`; their `ssh -p ...` has no `-oStrictHostKeyChecking=no`, so the first connection to every partner node (its host key is not in `known_hosts` yet, no terminal to answer) ended with "Host key verification failed", `activatetunnels.sh` counted the node as failed and finally declared "Remote cluster appears down". Both templates now pass `-oStrictHostKeyChecking=no` (the check ssh of the key exchange already did).
- **How the replication reaches the receiver:** the sender's etcd is exposed on the receiver cluster by `ssh -R <receiver cluster ip>:<port>:<sender etcd>`; the receiver's LEADER runs the user/group pull against its own cluster address, so the reverse tunnel has to end on the leader node (here: `Rremote_..._<leader node ip>_.sh`). With only the second node's tunnel up the leader answered "10.11.11.200 not reachable" and nothing was replicated; after the leader's tunnel was started the users and groups appeared on cluster 2 within a minute (unix users, groups with their members).

## 49. Replication: the receiver's "latest snapshot" and the sender mark, and slow share start — `QSD5.252` (2026-10-08)
Same test (`replication_1node_2transmitter-1recv`), after the tunnels worked:
- **`getlatestsnap.sh` looked at every snapshot with the volume's name (both flavours, only visible where both clusters see the same ZFS).** Run on the receiver, `zfs list -t snapshot | grep <volume>` also matches the sender's snapshots of the same volume name when sender and receiver share one ZFS namespace (the container flavour: one kernel for all node containers), so the "latest snapshot on the receiver" was the sender's own newest snapshot, `replicatenow.py` built an incremental stream from a snapshot to itself, the stream failed (`cannot receive: failed to read from stream`) and every replication ended with `Streamfa01`. `getlatestsnap.sh <volume> [<pool/volume>]` now takes the receiver's dataset as second argument (`replicatenow.py` passes `poolvol`) and counts only its snapshots. Verified: first stream full (new volume), second incremental `once1 -> once2`, the receiver dataset holds both snapshots and the files.
- **`setsnapsender.py` marked the wrong snapshot (same reason).** It found the snapshot by its bare name and put `partner:sender` on the sender's snapshot, so the Received Snapshots page of the receiver (it lists snapshots whose sender is set) stayed empty. `replicatenow.py` now passes the receiver's `pool/volume@snapshot` and the script uses it when given.
- **Share containers created together came up without samba users (both flavours).** `cifs.py` (§41) repeated the password step for 20 x 2 s; with two shares created at once the second container needed more than a minute. The window is 75 attempts (about 3 minutes).
- Observed, not changed: the admin account is never replicated (`usersyncall.py`: `'admin' != username`), so the admin password of the sending cluster is not accepted by the receiving cluster (the test expects it to be); `replicatenow.py` destroys the sender's snapshot when a stream fails (`zfs destroy -r pool/volume@snapshot`), and the typo `finalresonse` in it always selects the "noold" path.

## 50. Activating a replicated volume, and what a second cluster on the same kernel does — `QSD5.253` (2026-10-08)
Same test (`replication_1node_2transmitter-1recv`), receiver side:
- **A received volume was not mounted when it was plugged (both flavours).** `zfs recv` leaves the new dataset unmounted; `VolumeChangeCIFS` (activate = `statusmount=active`) started the share container, applied `chmod`/`setfacl` and exported the EMPTY mount point directory. It now runs `zfs mount <pool>/<volume>` first when the dataset is unmounted and the volume is being activated. Verified: after the plug the share lists the files of the replicated snapshot (usr1 sees r1..r3.txt, usr2 is denied as on the sender). `VolumeChangeNFS`/`...Home` were not changed (same gap, not tested).
- **The React CIFS list has no plug/unplug control.** The old UI sent `statusmount=active|false` to `volumes/config` from a plug icon; the current `CifsList.jsx` only edits ip, subnet and groups, so the replicated (red, not live) volume cannot be activated from the UI. Open (UI work).
- **Group membership did not reach the second node of the receiving cluster.** After the replication of users and groups the leader had `grp1: usr1`, the other node had `grp1:` without members (`usersigroup/grp1` empty there), so a share owned by that node denied the group's user. Fixed by hand in the test (key copied, `usermod -aG`); the sync gap is not fixed.

## 51. The sample-data API is part of the main line — `QSD5.254` (2026-10-08)
`TopStor/mockfapi.py` + the 4-line hook at the top of `fapi.py` (§34) now live in the normal code line instead of a separate `…u_mockfile` branch, so the UI-dev node `pzfs` runs the **latest QSD** and what is pushed from it is the next release.
- **Off by default.** `fapi.py` hands over to the mock only when `/TopStordata/mockapi` exists; without the file the real API runs. Switch on: `touch /TopStordata/mockapi` (host: `/home/topstor/pzfs/linux-env/TopStordata/mockapi`) and restart `fapi` (`docker exec pzfs docker restart flask`); switch off: remove the file, restart.
- **`QSD5.254` = `QSD5.253` + the mock** (TopStor only; pace and topstorweb are unchanged from 5.253). The route check: every `/api/v1` route of 5.253 `fapi.py` is answered by the mock (the `hosts/active|info|lost|possible|ready` handlers are commented-out routes, called inside `hosts/allinfo`). New answers of 5.238–5.253 (`poolhasvolumes`, `nopool`, `noprivilege`) are not simulated: the mock answers `Ok`.
- **Keeping it current:** when a release adds or changes a route, add the route and its sample answer to `mockfapi.py` in the same change; compare with `app.url_map` of `mockfapi` against the `route(` lines of `fapi.py`.
- The mock is shipped to every node but never runs unless the switch file exists.

## 52. Nodes page: equal-width node cards — `QSD5.255` (2026-10-08)
Front-end only (`topstorweb/src`, no API call changed). The node cards of *Running*, *Active* and *Discovered Nodes* were `w-fit` inside a flex-wrap row, so every card had the width of its own label (a node without alias, "node5", was narrower than "rack1-node1"). Now the three lists are a CSS grid (`grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-3 xl:grid-cols-4`), `ServerNode` fills its cell (`w-full min-w-0`), the name takes the free space (`flex-1 truncate`) so the Online/Offline label sits at the right edge of every card, and the fonts are smaller (name `text-xs`, status `10px`, address `11px`). Files: `Common/ServerNode.jsx`, `RunningNodes.jsx`, `ActiveNodes.jsx`, `DiscoveredNodes.jsx`.

## 53. Sample-data notifications, sync sign, Everyone group, logs by alias, sync now — `QSD5.256` (2026-10-08)
Front end (`topstorweb/src`) plus a small backend change (`fapi.py`, `UnixChangeUser`, `UnixChangeGroup`) and the mock (`mockfapi.py`, §51).
- **Notification toasts** (bottom right): compact (one title line "alias · user", one message line, the message code in 9 px grey for engineers). The title is the node's **alias** (name when the alias is empty or `_1`); the alias map comes from `hosts/allinfo`. The severity is the `type` field of `info/notification` (info|warning|error). The mock now rotates samples of all three severities every 7 s poll.
- **Sync sign** (next to the bell): one line, never wrapped. One ActivePartner (`hosts/allinfo` → `active`, re-read every 3rd poll) = blue led "Single node"; otherwise green "Cluster in Sync" or red "Nodes Not in Sync". The red sign is a **button: it calls `POST api/v1/hosts/syncnow`**, a new route that asks every ready node to run `/pace/checksyncs.py syncrequest <leaderip> <node> <nodeip>` now (the step each node's `syncrequestlooper` repeats). The 13 "Sync Now" page buttons (they only reloaded the page data) were removed. Mock: the state cycles every 5 minutes (min 0-2 in sync, 3 not in sync, 4 single node: only `active` shrinks); force it with the file `/TopStordata/mockphase` = `insync|notinsync|single`.
- **Group Everyone**: every user is always a member, the front end neither shows nor edits it (Users and Groups pages filter it out of the lists and of each user's assignments; the volume share-group pickers still show it). Backend: `with_everyone()` in `fapi.py` adds it to the group string of `UnixAddUser` and `userchange` (a user created, changed or imported through `UnixAddUser` always gets it); `UnixChangeUser` adds it itself when the group exists (sync, bulk upload); `groupchange`, `groupdel` and `UnixAddgroup` on Everyone answer `error: everyonefixed`; `UnixChangeGroup Everyone change` is ignored (the creation call still runs).
- **Logs** show the node **alias** (name when no alias), aliases refreshed at most every 30 s.

## 54. CIFS / NFS / Home pages: capacity, thin provisioning, compression and dedup choice, home folder goes with the user — `QSD5.257` (2026-10-08)
Competitor study (QNAP, Synology, Dell Unity / PowerScale, TrueNAS, NetApp): a short create form (name, pool, size, thin/thick, compression), and a list that shows used against limit, free space and what the pool can really back. Volumes here are always thin (a ZFS `quota`, no reservation); thick provisioning was declined by the maintainer.
- **List** (`components/ShareList.jsx`, wrapped by `CifsList`, `NfsList`, `HomeFoldersList`): Capacity (bar: data + snapshots, used / limit, %, amber from 75 %, red from 90 %; no quota = "no limit", the limit is what the pool has), Free, Snapshots (MB from the backend, shown in GB/MB), Efficiency (compression ratio plus Comp / Dedup badges from the volume properties), Access (`ip/subnet`, editable), Groups (CIFS/NFS, shown by name). Units from the backend: `used`, `quota`, `available` GB; `usedbysnapshots`, `referenced` MB.
- **Pool Capacity card** beside the create form (`PoolCapacityPanel` in `components/Common/Capacity.jsx`; data = `pools/dgsinfo` + `volumes/volumesinfo`): per pool real usage (`used` of `used + available`), provisioned (sum of the volume quotas, a volume without quota counts its `used`) and the over-provisioning ratio; over-provisioning is allowed and shown, not blocked.
- **Create forms** (CIFS, NFS, Home): the free space of the chosen pool, what is already provisioned and the total with the new volume; a note when the size is larger than the free space (allowed) and when the pool is above 90 %; **Compression (LZ4) and Deduplication are checked by default and may be unchecked**.
- **API / backend alignment:** `POST api/v1/volumes/create` takes `compression` and `dedup` (`on` | `off`, default `on`; also accepted: `false`/`no`/`0`). `fapi.py` appends `compression=<lz4|off> dedup=<on|off>` as the last words of the `VolumeCreateCIFS|CIFSdom|NFS|HOME` command (not for iSCSI); the scripts read them with `grep -o` wherever they stand and create the dataset with `-o dedup=$zdedup -o compression=$zcomp` (both on when the words are missing, so replication and older callers are unchanged). `pace/putzpool.py` lists the `compression` and `dedup` properties and reports them in each volume (`compression`, `dedup`) next to the existing fields.
- **90 % warning:** `capacitywarn()` in `pace/putzpool.py` (every pass of the pool scan, on the node that owns the pool): at used ≥ 90 % of `used + available` of the pool dataset it logs `Poolcap90` (warning, `msgsglobal.txt`; shows as a toast and in the log) and repeats every 2 hours while the pool stays above 90 %; the time of the last warning is `/TopStordata/capwarn_<pool>`.
- **Deleting a user deletes his home folder:** `userdel` in `fapi.py` now also sends `VolumeDeleteHOME <leaderip> <pool> <volume> HOME <user>` to the node that owns each HOME volume named `<user>_<id>` (not for `admin`); before, only the user went and the HOME dataset stayed.
- **Mock:** pool `pdhcp1003` at 94 % (alert + toast sample), `pdhcp1002` over-provisioned 1.19×, volumes with compression/dedup on and off, three home folders, a volume without quota.
- Not tested on a cluster: the create scripts, `putzpool.py` and the HOME delete need a run on the zfs cluster.

## 55. CIFS / NFS / Home lists edit like the users list — `QSD5.258` (2026-10-08)
Front end only (`topstorweb/src`, no API call changed). The row edit mode (pencil, check, x and a multi-line select) is gone. As in the users list, nothing is sent at once: a click on the **address** edits it in the row (address and subnet, the original value tiny and green above it, the changed value in amber, a small x takes it back), the **groups** field is the same compact multi select as in the users list (always there, a change is marked and has its own x), the trash icon marks a volume for deletion (row struck through, the arrow takes it back), and the **Submit changes** bar at the end sends everything: one `volumes/config` call per changed volume (`ipaddress` + `Subnet`, `groups` as names) and one `volumes/volumedel` per deleted volume, in order; Cancel drops all pending changes. The groups of a domain CIFS share are not editable (they come from the domain). Shared parts moved to `components/Common/PendingEdit.jsx` (`CurrentValue`, `RevertButton`, `OkButton`, `closeOnLeave`), also used by `UserList.jsx`; the list is `components/ShareList.jsx` (wrapped by `CifsList`, `NfsList`, `HomeFoldersList`), the submit logic is `handleSubmit` in `QCifs.jsx`, `QNfs.jsx`, `QHomeFolders.jsx`.

## 56. Everyone as a share group is exclusive — `QSD5.259` (2026-10-08)
Every user is a member of the group Everyone (§53), so as the group of a CIFS/NFS share it already means all users and the other groups add nothing. **Front end** (`components/Common/groupPick.js`, used by `QCifs.jsx`, `QNfs.jsx` and the groups field of `ShareList.jsx`): picking Everyone clears the other groups, picking another group while Everyone is selected takes Everyone out. **Backend:** `only_everyone()` in `fapi.py` makes the groups of `volumes/create` and `volumes/config` just `Everyone` when it is among them, and `VolumeCreateCIFS`, `VolumeChangeCIFS` and `VolumeChangeNFS` do the same with their group word (so an old caller or a direct command behaves the same). The share's directory ACL then gets `g:Everyone:rwx`, which reaches every user because §53 keeps all of them in that group. Existing volumes keep what they have until their groups are next changed.

The CIFS and NFS pages use the whole right pane (outer padding `p-3`, card padding `p-4`, was `p-5` / `p-6`), and on all three pages (CIFS, NFS, Home Folders) the *New Volume* card is two thirds of the row and the *Pool Capacity* card one third (`lg:grid-cols-3`, `lg:col-span-2`); the Pool Capacity header keeps the title on one line and shows the totals below it.

The Home Folders page now sits in the same container card as CIFS and NFS (it had `content-header px-4` and no card).

## 59. New Volume forms: compact rows and an address that must not collide — `QSD5.262` (2026-10-08)
**Layout** (CIFS, NFS, Home): row 1 = Serving (CIFS only, wide enough for "Workgroup"), Storage Pool (wide enough for `pdhcp123456`), Volume Name / user (takes the rest), **Size (GB)** (6 digits, up to 999999); row 2 = IP Address (just wide enough for an address), Subnet (just wide enough for 24) and, over each other beside them, the checkboxes (Compression, Deduplication; NFS also Active). NFS keeps its Root/Group row between the two. The free-space hint is one small line under row 2.
**Address check** (`components/Common/ipCheck.js`, used by the three forms, the Provision button is disabled while it fails and the message shows under the field): the address must not be the address of a node or the cluster; NFS shares share it with nothing; a **CIFS** share may share it only with CIFS shares of the **same context**, the workgroup or the same domain (volume `prot` is `CIFS` for the workgroup, `CIFS_<domain>` for a domain), so it is checked again at every key of the domain name (an empty domain name counts as a domain that no existing share has yet); never with NFS, home or iSCSI volumes; a home folder only with other homes. Data: `hosts/allinfo` + `volumes/volumesinfo` (`useCapacity` now also returns `volumes` and `hosts`). **Backend:** `ip_context()` in `fapi.py` makes `volumes/create` and `volumes/config` hand `is_unique_ip()` the etcd key text of the volumes that may share (`volumes/CIFS/` for the workgroup, `volumes/CIFS_<domain>/` for a domain, `ANYthing` = nobody for NFS); before, a workgroup share and a domain share (or two different domains) could share an address because the check left out every key containing `CIFS`. Partner addresses are still checked by the backend only.
Mock: a domain CIFS share (`payroll`, `CIFS_corp.local`, 10.11.11.218).

## 61. iSCSI page in the same theme as CIFS — `QSD5.264` (2026-10-08)
Front end only (`QIscsi.jsx`, `components/IscsiList.jsx` on top of `ShareList.jsx`, `Common/Capacity.jsx`, `Common/ipCheck.js`), the API calls are the same. Same container (no outer margin, square border, `p-2`), *Provision Block Device* two thirds and *Pool Capacity* one third (`gap-2`), same compact rows: Storage Pool, LUN Name, Size (GB) / IP Address, Subnet, Port, Active; the Initiators IQN text area stays below. The fields are the ones iSCSI had (no compression / dedup choice: a LUN is created with `-V`, both on). The address check applies with the LUN rule: a LUN shares an address only with other LUNs (one portal), never with a node, a share or a home folder. The free-space hint says a LUN reserves its whole size (`thick`).
**List:** same columns and way of editing as CIFS (`variant="iscsi"` of `ShareList`): Capacity (GB) / Free (GB) / Snapshots (GB) / Efficiency, then **IP:Port** (click to edit the address and the port 1024-65535) and **Allowed Initiators** (click to edit, IQNs separated by space, comma or new line; empty = `This_lun_is_not_mapped`), the trash marks a LUN for deletion, **Submit changes** sends one `volumes/config` (`ipaddress`, `portalport`, `initiators`) or `volumes/volumedel` per LUN. A LUN's capacity bar is the data written to it (`referenced`, MB) out of its size, because the whole size is reserved (`used` and `quota` are both the size).
Mock: a second LUN `dbstore`, written data for both.

## 62. Replication key exchange on a node without `/root/.ssh` — `QSD5.265` (2026-10-09)
Found by the QualityCheck test `replication_2node_1transmitter_2recv` (test 22, run on `QSD5.264`): steps 1-7 passed (two-node cluster 1, one-node cluster 2, users `usr1`/`usr2`, groups `grp1`/`grp2`, a Sender partner `Hqsite` in cluster 2 and a Receiver partner `DRsite` in cluster 1), **step 8 failed**: eight minutes after the partners were added cluster 2 still listed no users and only the group `Everyone`.
- **Root cause (both flavours).** The partner key exchange reaches the receiving node (`receivekeys.sh` ran: `/root/receivekeys` = `<node> <ip> <cluster ip> 2400 <phrase> ssh-ed25519_spc_...`, `it is okok`, `Port 2400` / `Port 22` in `sshd_config`, `nodesender/...` in etcd), but the script appends the sender's public key to `/root/.ssh/authorized_keys` and **the directory `/root/.ssh` does not exist on a node on which root never used ssh** (a fresh node, or a cluster that only receives). The `echo ... >> /root/.ssh/authorized_keys` failed silently, the key was never installed and the sender (`activatetunnels.sh` -> `initreplipartner.py`) got `Permission denied (publickey,...)`, `still closed` x10, `Remote cluster appears down`. Nothing was ever replicated, and the user/group push never started. A second effect: the repeated failed logins make OpenSSH 9.x (`PerSourcePenalties`) answer the sending node with `kex_exchange_identification: banner line 0: Not allowed at this time` for some minutes (another node with no failed logins still got the normal `Permission denied`), which only lengthens the outage.
- **Fix.** `receivekeys.sh` creates `/root/.ssh` (`mkdir -p`, mode 700) and an empty `authorized_keys` before it reads and extends the file. Nothing else in the exchange (`preparekeys.sh`, `sendreceivekeys.py`, `initreplipartner.py`) writes under `/root/.ssh` of the receiver.
- **Verified live** (cluster 2 = `zfs3`, cluster 1 = `zfs1` + `zfs2`): the changed file copied into the receiver's tree, `activatetunnels.sh 10.11.11.200` run on the sender: `/root/.ssh` (700) and `authorized_keys` (the sender's key) appeared on `zfs3`, the tunnel scripts `Lremote_/Rremote_DRsite_Receiver_<node ip>_.sh` started (`ssh -N -L 10.11.11.200:2390:10.11.11.100:2379` and `-R`), and within a minute cluster 2 listed `usr1` (groups 0,1), `usr2` (groups 0,2) and `Everyone`, `grp1`, `grp2` with the same members as cluster 1 (`id usr1` / `id usr2` on the receiver show `grp1` / `grp2`).
- **Open (found by the same test, not fixed here):** *group membership given while a user is created is lost on the other nodes of the cluster.* `UnixAddUser` on the leader files two sync requests a few nanoseconds apart (`user` and `UsrChange`); the follower creates the user from the first one (`UnixChangeUser` with the user's own group and `Everyone` only) and the `UsrChange` copy (`UnixChangeUser ... groupsgrp2,Everyone ... pullsync`) is processed while the user does not exist yet (`id $username` fails and the script ends), so `grp1` / `grp2` stayed empty on the second node (`usersigroup/grp1` = `NoUser` in its local etcd) and did not heal in ten minutes. Re-sending the groups with `POST users/userchange` (Edit user) fixed it in 5 s. Proposed fix: make the `user` sync path of `UnixAddUser` / `oneusersync` apply the groups from the leader's etcd (or re-queue the `UsrChange` request until the user exists).

## 63. Finding: the admin password of the sending cluster is not replicated (test 23, `QSD5.265`, 2026-10-09) — no code change
QualityCheck test `replication_single_node_clusters` (test 23, `QSD5.265`, two single-node clusters): steps 1-7 passed (the step-8 bug of test 22 is fixed: `/root/.ssh` is created, the tunnels come up and `usr1`, `usr2`, `grp1`, `grp2` arrived on the receiver by themselves), **step 8 failed**: "logon to c2node_1 with the admin password of the c1" — `GET /api/v1/login?user=admin&pass=<cluster 1 admin password>` on the receiver answers `baduser`, while the replicated user `usr1` logs in there.
- **Why.** The user replication (`pace/usersyncall.py`, `thread_add`) walks the sender's `usersinfo/*` keys and creates each user with its `usershash/<user>` on the receiver. `admin` has `usershash/admin` and `usershashadm/admin` but no `usersinfo/admin`, so it is never sent. The only other path is the `passwd` sync (`checksyncs.py`, `special1`, in `forReceivers`), which runs `UnixChangePass <user> <requester>` and reads the hash from the node's OWN etcd (`usershash/<user>`), i.e. it only makes the nodes of one cluster follow a password change; it never carries the hash across to a partner cluster. `PartnerAdd.py` writes `pushusers = <alias>/<cluster ip>`, but no script reads that key.
- **Proposed change (not made: it replaces the DR site's admin password, a design/security decision, and touches `promserver.sh` / the `AdminStor` comment of the unix account).** In the receiver's `pullsync` pass of `usersyncall`, also read `usershash/admin` from the sender (`getnoport(leaderip, pport, 'usershash/admin')`) and, only when the partner is of type Sender and the receiver is configured to accept it, store it as `usershash/admin` on the receiver leader (+ `usermod -p` / `-c"AdminStor"<hash>` through `UnixChangePass`), then let the normal `passwd` sync carry it to the receiver's other nodes. Alternatively make the Replication page say that the admin password is NOT replicated and change the test text.
- **Verified:** receiver `usershash/admin` differs from the sender's; the receiver's own admin password still works; the sender's is rejected; no pushed code is affected.

## 64. The admin password of the sending cluster follows to the DR (receiving) cluster — `QSD5.266` (2026-10-09)
Maintainer decision after §63 (test 23, step 8, "logon to c2node_1 with the admin password of the c1"): the receiving cluster takes the sender's admin password. Changes, all in `pace/` (both flavours, python only):
- **`usersyncall.pulladminhash(username)`** (new): reads `usershash/<user>` from the sender's etcd through the replication tunnel (`getnoport(leaderip, pport, ...)`), and when it differs from the receiver's own it stores it as `usershash/<user>` in the receiver leader's etcd and queues the normal `sync/passwd/UnixChangePass_<user>_admin/request`, so every node of the receiver applies it (`UnixChangePass` reads the hash from the node's etcd, sets the unix password and the `AdminStor` comment, restarts the Prometheus login). The hash is encrypted with a key that depends only on the user name, so it is valid on any cluster. Only for `admin` and for users that already exist on the receiver (their `usersinfo`); a stray `usershash` key is never created.
- **Initial replication:** `usersyncall(pullsync)` (the `user` initial sync of a new partnership) calls it for `admin` after the users are pulled.
- **Later changes:** `checksyncs.replisyncrequest`, branch `special1` (`passwd`), calls `pulladminhash(<user>)` before it runs `UnixChangePass`; before, the receiver ran `UnixChangePass` against its own, unchanged hash.
- **Older bug found on the way (fixed):** `replisyncrequest` called `synckeysnoport(...)` for every `passwd` sync, but the name was never imported (and `etcdsyncnoport.synckeysnoport` itself is unfinished: undefined `noport`, ignores the tunnel port, deletes the receiver's local `Partner` keys before copying) so every pulled password change ended the whole pull with `NameError: name 'synckeysnoport' is not defined` (`/root/syncreqerr.log` on the receiver); the call is now skipped for `passwd` (the copy of `sync/passwd` keys has no use there). The `Partnr` branch of that block is still unreachable (`Partnr` is not in `forReceivers`); `etcdsyncnoport.py` stays unfinished.
- **Verified live** (two single-node clusters, sender `zfs3` 10.11.11.100, receiver `zfs1` 10.11.11.200): (1) the sender's admin password changed with `POST hosts/config username=admin password=...` after the pairing: the new password logged in on the receiver 15 s after the pull ran, before the fix `baduser` for ever (the NameError above); (2) the receiver's admin set to a different password by hand (the sender's password rejected), then the initial-sync code (`usersyncall('pullsync')` + `groupsyncall('pullsync')` through the live tunnel) run: `pulladminhash: the password of admin follows the sending cluster`, the sender's password logs in, the receiver's own old one is rejected; users and group memberships unchanged afterwards.
- **Open:** a receiver cluster with SEVERAL nodes: the non-leader nodes get the new hash from the `passwd` sync of their own leader (`UnixChangePass` reads `usershash/admin` from the local etcd) — not tested here. The user/`UsrChange` sync race of §62 (group membership at user creation) is fixed in §65 (`QSD5.267`).

## 65. Group membership given while a user is created reaches every node — `QSD5.267` (2026-10-09)
Closes the open point of §62 (found by test 22, group `grp1`/`grp2` empty on the second node of the cluster). Two causes, both in the sync of a new user:
- **Order of the requests (`pace/checksyncs.py`, both `syncrequest` and `replisyncrequest`).** A follower processes its pending sync requests sorted by `value.split('_')[1]`. The value is `user_<name>_<stamp>` for the user but `UsrChange_<stamp>` for the change of its groups, so the key was the user NAME for one and the stamp for the other; digits sort before letters, so the group change was always processed BEFORE the user existed on the node (`UnixChangeUser` ends with `id $username` failing) and was dropped. New key `reqorder(item)`: the time the request was filed, as integer nanoseconds (the last `_` field; seconds / milliseconds are scaled, `passwd_<s.fraction>` handled, `*_initial_*` first). `user_` now runs before `UsrChange_`, `group_` before `GrpChange_`, in the order they were made.
- **A malformed second request (`TopStor/UnixAddUser`).** After the user's own request the leader filed `sync/UsrChange/UnixChangeUser_$@ s$pullsync`, where `$@` is the argument list of UnixAddUser (`leaderip user NoHome groupsX password size addr subnet hoststub requester`), so followers ran `UnixChangeUser <leaderip> <user> NoHome groupsX Passw0rd12 ...` (groups = `NoHome`, requester = `groupsX,Everyone`). It was invisible while the order bug dropped it. The correct request (`UnixChangeUser <leaderip> <user> groupsX <requester> create <stamp>` with the stamp 10 s ahead) is already filed by the `UnixChangeUser` call that UnixAddUser makes for the leader; the malformed copy is removed.
- **Verified live** (two-node cluster `zfs1` + `zfs2`, 10.11.11.200): before (zfs2 on the old `pace`): `usrA` created in `grpA` -> on `zfs2` the unix user exists, `id usrA` has only `Everyone`, `usersigroup/grpA` = `NoUser` after 120 s (zfs1 had it in 5 s). After the new `checksyncs.py` / `UnixAddUser` on zfs2: five more users (`usrC`..`usrF`, one with a capture of the follower log) each in their own group: `id` on zfs2 shows the group 0-10 s after the leader, `usersigroup/grpC..grpF` list the user in zfs2's local etcd; the follower log shows `UnixAddUser` (user), then the group change, in that order. (`usrB`, created seconds after the file was copied while the previous loop still ran the old code, was lost as before.)
- **Not covered:** a user created while a node is down and returns later (the node replays its pending requests in the same, now correct, order); not run on the physical flavour (python/shell only, no flavour guard touched).

## 66. A failed first import after a take over no longer orphans the pool — `QSD5.268` (2026-10-09)
Found by the QualityCheck test `users_2nodes_OneCluster` (test 26, `QSD5.267`), step "Wait till the Web 10.11.11.249 loads again ... users, groups, volumes are all shown": after the primary (leader AND pool owner) was closed, the portal returned from the survivor in 10 s with all users and groups, but **no volume was ever shown** and the pool stayed unimported (`zpool import` listed it `DEGRADED`, importable, one mirror leg `UNAVAIL`). Step failed (`on_failure: stop`, test ended).
- **Root cause (both flavours).** `zpooltoimport.py` runs on the leader every 9 s. `poolnxt/<pool>` (the host that must take the pool) is its only trigger, and the code **deleted `poolnxt/<pool>` BEFORE running `zpool import`** (and once more after the loop, whatever the result). When the first attempt failed — here 9 s after the leader change, before the survivor's disk was reachable again — the trigger was gone for ever: `selectimport` only assigns pools that still have a record in `pools/`, and `remknown.py` had just deleted the lost node's `pools/`, `volumes/` and `poolnxt` records. Nothing ever retried; `etcdgetlocal pools|poolnxt|volumes` on the survivor were empty and the portal showed no volume although the pool, its datasets and the data were intact.
- **Fix.** `pace/zpooltoimport.py`: `poolnxt/<pool>` is deleted only after the import worked (`pool in zpool status` and ONLINE/DEGRADED); a failed attempt removes only the provisional `pools/<pool>` record and leaves `poolnxt`, so the next round (9 s) tries again.
- **Reproduced and verified live** (two-node cluster, a mirror pool with one disk on each node, 5 CIFS + 5 HOME shares; both nodes switched so that the closed node is leader + owner + holder of the host `iscsid`): before: pool never imported, 5 minutes of `kernelpools=[] poolnxt=0 pools=0 volumes=0` on the survivor. After: first attempt at 10:17:19 failed (`pools/<pool>` appeared and was removed again, `poolnxt` kept), the retry at 10:17:33 imported the pool (`poolnxt` removed), `VolumeCheck` rebuilt the `volumes/` records, and 14 s later the survivor ran all 10 share containers; `GET volumes/CIFS|HOME/volumesinfo` listed 5 + 5, all `active serviceok`, pool ONLINE. (Control: when the survivor is already the leader the first attempt works, ~15 s after the stop.)
- **Open:** `remknown.py` still deletes the lost node's `pools/` / `volumes/` / `poolnxt` records at once; the pool is then rediscovered by the import (`VolumeCheck` rebuilds `volumes/` from the datasets), so for a few seconds the volume list of the portal is empty after a take over — expected, not a failure. A pool with **no** `poolnxt` assignment at all (assignment never synced to the follower) is still not imported by `zpooltoimport.py`; `selectimport` assigns it only while `pools/<pool>` exists.

## 67. RAID 50 was created as a single-parity group — `QSD5.269` (2026-10-09)
Found by the QualityCheck test `diskgroups_2nodes` (test 10, `QSD5.268`, step "Create RAID 50 using 10 x 10GB Disks"): `POST pools/newpool redundancy=raid50 useable=64.2 cache_bool=false` answered HTTP 200 but **no pool was ever created** (`DGst17` "Creating redundant Pool : using single parity array" then `DGfa17` "Failed creating ..."; `zpool list` empty after 300 s). Step failed, test ended.
- **Root cause (both flavours).** `fapi.py` builds the `DGsetPool` command with an `elif` chain on `data['redundancy']`: `elif 'raid5' in ...: 'parity'` came BEFORE `elif 'raid50' in ...: 'raid50'`, and `'raid5'` is a substring of `'raid50'`, so a RAID50 request was sent as `parity` (one single-parity raidz1 over all nine disks) and failed; the `raid50` branch of `DGsetPool` (three raidz1 groups of three disks) was never reached. Same order in `addtopool` (`addparity` before `addraid50`: adding a RAID50 group to a pool). (`raid60` / `raid6` and `raid6plus` / `raid6` were already in the right order.) Proof: `/root/tmp2` of `DGsetPool` on the owner started with `10.11.11.200 parity admin ...` for a `raid50` request.
- **Fix.** `TopStor/fapi.py`: `elif 'raid5' in data['redundancy'] and 'raid50' not in data['redundancy']:` in both places (`newpool`, `addtopool`).
- **Verified live** (two nodes, 12 loop disks): the same request now reaches `DGsetPool` as `raid50 ...`, `DGst17` then `DGsu17` 23 s later, pool ONLINE, 88.5 GB, `avail:type=raid50`, `zpool status`: `raidz1-0`, `raidz1-1`, `raidz1-2` of three disks each, no errors; deleted again with `pools/delpool` (all disks free after 10 s). (The first retry right after a hand-made test pool on the same disks failed once with `cannot open .../...-part1: Device or resource busy`, `/root/dgcreateerror`; the next attempt a minute later worked — a transient hold of the devices after a destroy, not seen again.)
- **Open (not changed):** the card of that pool reads *Highly Available, not balanced*: `selectraid50` put `raidz1-0` entirely on node 1 and `raidz1-2` entirely on node 2 (5 + 4 disks chosen), so the loss of a node kills a group. With two nodes a 3-disk raidz1 group cannot have one disk per node; the test text expects "Highly Available - Balanced" for RAID50 / RAID60, which needs either groups of 2+1 disks per node or three nodes. To be decided with the maintainer; the test step "Wait till the new pool is 'highly available - Balanced'" for RAID50 is likely to fail for that reason.

## 68. A user with the Node Config privilege was refused by the backend — `QSD5.270` (2026-10-09)
Found by the QualityCheck test `privileges_2nodes` (test 11, `QSD5.269`, second pass, step "relogon with admin and set usr1 privileged to the Node Config and check"): `usersinfo/usr1` held `Error-true` and the privilege list showed it ON, but `POST hosts/config` as `usr1` still answered `error: noprivilege`. Step failed, test ended.
- **Classification (regression of an earlier fix).** The enforcement was added in `QSD5.247` (§ "Node Config privilege was not enforced"): `has_privilege()` in `fapi.py` shelled out to `/TopStor/privthis.sh`. That was checked for the refusal (a user WITHOUT the privilege) and for admin, never for a user that HAS the privilege.
- **Root cause (both flavours).** The API runs inside the `flask` container (`docker exec flask /TopStor/fapi.py`). There `privthis.sh` cannot work: `/bin/sh` is dash (`[[: not found`) and there is no `docker` CLI (`docker: not found`), so it prints `false` for every non-admin user. The same script on the node answers `true`.
- **Fix.** `fapi.py` `has_privilege(priv, user)`: `admin` / `system` always; any other user needs the flag `<priv>-true` in `usersinfo/<user>`, read from etcd with the module's own `get()` (regex on the `/`-separated flags, same rule as `privthis.sh`). Used by `hosts/config` and `hosts/joincluster`.
- **Verified live** (fresh two-node cluster): `usr1` with `Box_Users` + `Error` -> `hosts/config` accepted; `usr2` with no privilege -> `noprivilege`; `usr1` before the privilege was set -> `noprivilege`; admin accepted. Tool `scripts/qc-harness/privcheck.sh <user> <password>` shows the privileges, the gated menu entries the UI shows for them (rules of `Sidebar.jsx`) and the two backend probes.
- **Open:** the backend enforces only Node Config; other privileges (Users & Groups, Logs, CIFS ...) are enforced by the front end menu only (`users/userlist` answers any logged-in user). Not changed here.

## 69. `showmount -e` against an NFS volume hung — `QSD5.271` (2026-10-09)
Found by the QualityCheck test `nfs_2node` (test 12, `QSD5.270`, second pass, step "Check NFS export availability: showmount -e 10.11.11.240"). It had been recorded as "not changed, by design" in §44 (the volumes are NFSv4-only).
- **Classification (not a regression, not a lost fix).** A known limit of the NFSv4-only image that the test checks. The tester was later told that `showmount` does not apply to NFSv4 volumes, so this is **N/A for the test**; the change below is an optional extra that does not touch NFSv4 mounts.
- **Root cause.** Two things: `rpc.mountd` ran with `--no-nfs-version 3` and a random port, and the `rpcbind` inside the NAT'd NFS container answers GETADDR (v3/v4) with the address the request arrived on, i.e. the container's private `172.17.0.x`; `showmount`/`rpcinfo` then waited in SYN_SENT on it. Registering mountd with the public address in rpcbind does not help (rpcbind rewrites the host part).
- **Fix.** `TopStor/nfsd.sh` (bind-mounted over the image's script): mountd v3 on fixed port 20048, nfsd stays v4-only. `nfsnew.sh` publishes 20048 and starts `TopStor/nfsportmap.py <ip> <container>` on the volume ip: a portmap v2 answerer on 111 (tcp+udp; NULL, GETPORT, DUMP) that refuses v3/v4 with PROG_MISMATCH so libtirpc falls back to GETPORT, which carries no address. It ends when its container is gone.
- **Verified live.** `showmount -e 10.11.11.240` from the client lists the export, `rpcinfo -p` lists portmapper/mountd/nfs, `mount -o vers=4` and file access unchanged; the full test 12 re-run passed (steps 17-30: users, ids, pool delete refused while volumes exist, NFS delete, second node join with balance in 20 s, node 1 stop with take over, copy after take over). Tools: `scripts/qc-harness/nfsrecreate.sh`, `nfsvm.sh`.

## 70. Create buttons of the iSCSI / NFS / CIFS pages skipped the form validation — `QSD5.272` (2026-10-09)
Found by the QualityCheck test `iscsi-2nodes` (test 13, `QSD5.271`, first pass, step 5 "Create an empty ISCSI Volume"; steps 6-8 are the same defect). Step 5 failed and the platform ended the test.
- **Classification (new bug).** Not in the earlier cycles of the iSCSI test; the same pattern is in the NFS and CIFS pages, whose checks passed only because the backend refused the request.
- **Symptom.** An empty or incomplete form gave NO message: the pool is not a form field, the click handler threw on the missing pool and swallowed it; with a name or IP missing the request `volumes/create?type=ISCSI&...&name=&...` WAS sent and the user saw the misleading toast "The name is already in use."
- **Root cause (both flavours).** `QIscsi.jsx` / `QNfs.jsx` / `QCifs.jsx`: the submit `Button` has `onClick={handleCreate}` beside the form `onSubmit`; the click runs the handler directly with `e.preventDefault()`, so the browser's required-field validation of the form never ran.
- **Fix (topstorweb/src only).** `handleCreate` first calls `form.reportValidity()` (shows the field messages and stops) and, for the pool dropdown, sets the banner "Select a storage pool first".
- **Verified live** (headless browser on the rebuilt UI, `scripts/qc-harness/ui-tests/iscsiui.sh fill ...`): empty form, no pool, no IP and no name all send no request; the field bubbles / the banner show. UI rebuilt on zfs1 (`index-BSWjQ-o5.js`). Tools: `iscsiui.sh`, `pushbranch.sh <BRANCH>`.

## 71. Any initiator could log in to an iSCSI target — `QSD5.273` (2026-10-09)
Found while running `iscsi-2nodes` (test 13, `QSD5.271`, steps 11-13, Windows initiator); not a step of the test, reported by the tester's own check of the LIO setup.
- **Classification (old design flaw, not a regression).** `pace/addzfsvolumeastarget.sh` has always set `generate_node_acls=1` on the target portal group.
- **Symptom.** The LUN's "Allowed Initiators" (the ACL created for the listed IQN) was not enforced: LIO with `generate_node_acls=1` gives any other initiator name a dynamic ACL that maps every LUN. A raw login with `iqn.1991-05.com.microsoft:other` was accepted (status class 0), same as the listed `...:win10`.
- **Fix.** `addzfsvolumeastarget.sh`: `generate_node_acls=0`, so only the ACLs created for the LUN's initiators may log in. A LUN created without initiators (`This_lun_is_not_mapped`) is unreachable until an initiator is added, as intended.
- **Verified live** (zfs2 owns the pool after the node 1 test): `targetcli ... get attribute generate_node_acls` = 0 on the re-created target; `scripts/qc-harness/iscsilogin.py 10.11.11.210 3260 <target> <iqn>`: listed IQN accepted (class 0), unlisted IQN refused (class 2, detail 2 = not authorized). Targets that already exist keep the old setting until their LUN is re-created or re-activated.
- **Open (not changed).** After the last LUN of a target is removed (step 15) the empty target `iqn.2016-03.com.<ip>:data`, its portal and the secondary IP stay on the node; a login succeeds but exposes no LUN.

## 72. `smbuserfix.sh` could not be executed: no samba user in a new CIFS share — `QSD5.274` (2026-10-09)
Found by the QualityCheck test `snapshots_2nodes` (test 14, `QSD5.273`, second pass, step 6 "Create some CIFs and assign to grp1 and copy one file ... using usr1"): `smbclient -U usr1%<password>` answered `NT_STATUS_LOGON_FAILURE`, `pdbedit -L` in the share container was empty. Local run only: the platform step is not reached yet.
- **Classification (the §41 fix does not hold; old defect, not a regression).** §41 (`QSD5.244`) made `cifs.py` copy `smbuserfix.sh` to `/etc` and retry `docker exec <CIFS> /hostetc/smbuserfix.sh x <user> <pass>` until `pdbedit` lists the user. That code is deployed and runs, but the script itself starts with `#/bin/sh` (missing `!`, since 2021): `docker exec` answers `exec /hostetc/smbuserfix.sh: exec format error` on this image, so every attempt fails and no user is ever added (the retry loop only hides it). The earlier pass of that step therefore did not come from this path.
- **Fix.** `TopStor/smbuserfix.sh`: first line `#!/bin/sh`.
- **Verified live.** Share deleted and created again (`rcreatecifs`, grp1): `pdbedit -L` lists usr1, usr2, usr3 within 6 s of the container start, with no manual step; `smbclient //10.11.11.211/<share> -U usr1%Passw0rd12 -c 'put ...'` succeeds, usr2 (not in grp1) gets `NT_STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED`.
- **Side findings (not changed).** The CIFS page defaults "Serving" to Domain and accepts empty Domain/xDC fields: a volume created that way had no groups and stayed `servicedown`. The host `iscsid.socket` can be socket-activated by host-side `iscsiadm` calls and then blocks the new node's own iscsid (test environment only, see memory note).

## 73. Empty share configuration right after a take over — `QSD5.275` (2026-10-09)
Found by the QualityCheck test `snapshots_2nodes` (test 14, `QSD5.274`, step 20 "Check the cifs if the file-x is still there"): after node 1 took the pool back, `smbclient //10.11.11.211/<share>` showed an empty share although the dataset held the files.
- **Cause.** `VolumeCheck.py` starts `cifs.py` when a volume is dirty, 8 s before the pool import had finished. `cifs.py` read `/<pool>/smb.<volume>` while the dataset was not mounted, skipped the read error (`except: continue`) and started the share container with an empty `smb.conf`; nothing started it again.
- **Fix.** `TopStor/cifs.py`: before the configuration is built it waits (90 x 2 s) until `zfs list -o mounted` says `yes` and `/<pool>/smb.<volume>` exists; if the dataset never comes it starts nothing, the volume stays dirty and the next volume check starts it again.
- **Verified live.** Share container removed and started again by `VolumeCheck` after a take over: `testparm` lists the share, `smbclient ... ls` shows the files.
- **Regression note (found in cycle with `QSD5.276`).** `QSD5.275` was branched from `QSD5.273` instead of `QSD5.274`, so it did not contain §72 (the `smbuserfix.sh` shebang): the run on `QSD5.275` showed "samba users NOT set" again. A new `QSD5.<N+1>` branch must start from the latest pushed branch; since then it is checked in the QC skill.

## 74. The pool id was not changed after an import on a degraded pool: stale disks could be imported again — `QSD5.276` (2026-10-09)
User directive: a pool is imported by its **id** (not its name); after the import the id is changed (`zpool reguid`) and synced to all nodes, so that the next import takes the newest id and an old disk can never be imported as the pool. Found while looking at lost data after the second take over of test 14 (`file-x` and the Minutely snapshots written while node 2 owned the pool were missing).
- **What the code did.** `pace/zpooltoimport.py` imports with `zpool import <ActPool/<pool>>`, runs `zpool reguid`, stores the new id as `ActPool/<pool>` and syncs it (`dosync('actpool_', 'sync/ActPool/Add_<pool>_<guid>/request', ...)`). When `reguid` was refused the id read back was the old one, it was stored and synced again as if it were new, and the retry marker `poouids/<pool>` (read at the top of `zpooltoimport()`) was never set (its `put` was commented out). A pool imported degraded (the missing disk of the other node is still in it) refuses `reguid`: proved on a throw-away pool: `zpool reguid` succeeds on a healthy mirror and fails on a degraded one with `cannot reguid 'rgtest': one or more devices is currently unavailable`. The stale disk therefore kept the same id as the live pool.
- **Fix.** `pace/zpooltoimport.py`: `zpool reguid` runs with its stderr captured. On success: old `sync/ActPool` request removed, `ActPool/<pool>` stored, synced, retry marker removed. On refusal: message `reguid refused (pool not healthy yet), retried later`, the old id stays published, the retry marker `poouids/<pool>` is set. The retry loop at the top of `zpooltoimport()` runs `zpool reguid` as soon as the pool is online (the missing disk replaced or detached) and then publishes and syncs the new id; a marker for a pool this node does not own is deleted.
- **Verified live (run 143, `QSD5.276`).** First take over (node 2): `zpool import pdhcp...` then `zpool reguid` 1 s later (pool healthy). Second take over (node 1): `zpool import 9411395270669872792` (by id, the id stored by node 2), `zpool detach` of the dead disk at 01:01:55, `zpool reguid` at 01:02:00 (the retry); the pool id afterwards, `18388502835563169720`, equals `ActPool/pdhcp1462232241`. A marker file written straight into the dataset on node 2 (`file-x-direct.txt`) survived both take overs (`VERDICT DATASET_FILEX_OK`), the Minutely snapshots of the 2-minute schedule were there.

## 75. The discovery etcd was started with an empty address; the share container died after a take over and nobody restarted it — `QSD5.277` (2026-10-10)
Found by the QualityCheck test `snapshots_2nodes` (test 14, local re-runs on `QSD5.276`): (a) the join of node 2 hung for 10+ minutes, (b) step 20 "Check the cifs if the file-x is still there" failed after the second take over: `smbclient` answered `NT_STATUS_CONNECTION_REFUSED` for 5+ minutes.
- **(a) `getdiscovery.sh`.** It starts the `discovery` container, waits a fixed `sleep 3` and reads the container's address from the internal DNS (`nslookup discovery`). On a busy node (the other node is booting) the answer came later, `newip` was empty, `/TopStordata/discovery.sh` got `etcdip=''`, the discovery etcd never ran and the scan polled the dead port 600 rounds; the second scan was refused by the "already running" guard, the joining node announced itself to nobody. Fix: wait up to 60 s for the address; if none, remove the container, undo the extra address and exit 1; the scan loop also stops when the `discovery` container is gone. Verified: `discovery Up`, `etcdip='10.11.12.9'`, `possible/<node2>` present 3 minutes after the start of node 2.
- **(b) `cifs.py`.** `dockerd.log`: `22:02:01 sbJoin ... ep=CIFS-10.11.11.211`, `22:02:03 Error setting up exec command in container CIFS-10.11.11.211: container ... is not running`: the share container (started with `--rm`, so its logs are gone) died within 2 s of its start. `cifs.py` went on with the samba password loop (75 tries x 2 s per user) against a container that did not exist, and `VolumeCheck.py`, which waits for `cifs.py`, could not repair anything for 7+ minutes. Fix: `cifs.py` starts the container (`cifs.sh`) again until `docker ps` shows it up 8 s later (5 tries), writes the output of every try to `/root/cifsrun.log`, gives up with a message after the 5th, and the password loop stops when the container is gone. The cause of the early death is not known (the new log will show it).
- **Verified live.** Container killed 3 s after its start: back up with usr1/usr2/usr3 in 12 s. Container killed continuously for 45 s: `cifs.py` made 5 tries 9 s apart, logged each, answered `share container did not stay up after 5 tries` after 47 s (before: no end for minutes); once the killer stopped the share came back by itself and `smbclient` listed all files. Full run 144: join 2 min 37 s, balanced after 32 s, `VERDICT DATASET_FILEX_OK` and `VERDICT FILEX_OK` (file-x copied through samba survived both take overs), Minutely snapshots there; local re-run of steps 20-24 passed (`qc-step-times.csv`).
- **Harness findings (tools, not product).** `join.sh` read the hostname of node 2 right after `docker start`, when `docker exec` still fails: the error text stayed in `$H` and the discovery check never matched (join hung 5+ min); it now waits for a real `dhcp<digits>` name. `test14auto.sh` retries file copies and share checks for 2 minutes (the share needs about a minute after a take over) and logs the share container and `/root/cifsrun.log` when it is missing.
- **Open finding (not changed).** When node 1 returned (`docker_setup.container.sh`, `cmyrepopull.sh $leaderversion`) it switched its tree to branch `QSD5.276` (`docker_setup.log`: `Switched to and reset branch 'QSD5.276'`, `pace: couldn't find remote ref refs/heads/QSD5.276`) although the leader was on `QSD5.277` and `cversion/<both nodes>` read `QSD5.277-c365b29d`; `return.sh` reported `TopStor differs: zfs2 c365b29d zfs1 6cee7a71`. The value of `leaderversion` at that moment is not recorded; to be looked at with the next return.

## 76. A user could delete the files of another user on a CIFS share — `QSD5.278` (2026-10-10)
Found by the QualityCheck test `cifs_domain_2nodes` (test 16, `QSD5.277`, step 24 "from within win2 try to delete file1.txt"): `QC\usr2` deleted `fil1.txt` created by `QC\usr1`. The maintainer asked for the opposite default.
- **Classification (old design, not a regression).** `VolumeActivateCIFSdom` set the share directory to `777`; with write permission on the directory any domain user may unlink any file in it. The workgroup shares have the same property (group `rwx` directory `770`/`2770`, any member of the share group can delete the others' files).
- **Fix.** The sticky bit on the share directory: only the owner of a file (or the directory owner / root, i.e. the share's administrator) can delete or rename it. `VolumeActivateCIFSdom`: `chmod 1777`; `VolumeActivateCIFS`: `chmod 1770`; `VolumeCreateCIFS`: `chmod 3770` (set-group-id kept as before). Applies to new shares and, because the activation runs at every take-over / start, to existing shares at their next activation.
- **Verified live (both flavours' tooling is the same scripts).** Domain volume `dom10` created again: directory `drwxrwxrwt`; `QC\usr1` puts `fil1.txt`, `QC\usr2` `del fil1.txt` -> `NT_STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED`, `QC\usr1` deletes its own file. Workgroup volume `wg1` (group grp1 with usr1 and usr2): directory `drwxrws--T`, usr2 delete of usr1's file refused, usr1 deletes it.

## 77. Replication tunnels did not reach the receiver's leader; another cluster's pool was adopted in the shared kernel — `QSD5.279` (2026-10-10)
Found by the QualityCheck test `replication_1node_2transmitter-1recv` (test 21, `QSD5.278`; cluster 1 = zfs3, cluster 2 = zfs1 + zfs2, both in the same host kernel).
- **(a) Tunnels (`TopStor/activatetunnels.sh`).** The sender keeps ssh -R tunnels to the receiver; the receiver's LEADER pulls through its own cluster address, so the tunnel must end on the receiver's leader node. The script only started the tunnels of the "readyonly" entries, so after the partners were added the tunnel to the receiver leader (10.11.11.201) did not exist and the users/groups did not replicate. Fix: after the existing block it reads the partner's `leader` and `ready/<leader>` from the partner's etcd and starts `Lremote_*`/`Rremote_*` to that address when the files exist and no such ssh is running. Verified live: partners deleted and added again, the tunnels to .201 came up within about 30 s and the users replicated.
- **Operational note (not a product change).** The partner password is a shared secret and must be identical on both clusters (`receivekeys.sh` greps the Partner record for the received password). Different passwords made the key exchange stop silently.
- **(b) Cross-cluster adoption (`TopStor/getvols.sh`).** All containers share ONE kernel, so a pool imported by cluster 1 is visible and mounted in cluster 2's nodes. `getvols.sh` listed `/pdhcp*/smb.*`, so cluster 2's `VolumeCheck` registered cluster 1's volume under its own node (`volumes/CIFS/<c2 host>/<c1 pool>/<volume>`, active) and started a second `CIFS-<ip>` container that held cluster 1's dataset: the pool could not be exported (`pool is busy`), and stopping zfs2 (host iscsid holder) was refused. Fix: in the container flavour `getvols.sh` lists only the pools the node owns (`cpoolowner.sh mine $(hostname)`); physical servers keep the glob. Verified live: each node lists only its own volumes.
- **Open finding.** After c1's pool was exported and imported again, cluster 2 wrote `poolnxt/`, `ActPool/` and `pools/` entries for it again (`sync/ActPool/Add_<pool>_...`). The owner property stayed with cluster 1, so there was no damage, but the pool-import selection needs the same "mine" guard (container flavour only). Removed by hand.
- **Open finding.** After the cluster 2 leader changed, the admin password was the default again (the replicated/changed one was only on the dead node).
- **Harness.** `replisciscross.sh` (explicit rw ACL for the iscsid container's initiator, `OWN=` auto-detect), `lib.sh` `wait_eth10` 900 s, `resetcluster.sh` `RESUME2=1`.
- **Result.** Test 21 passed (all steps) with the workarounds above for the kernel-wide iscsid (c1 pool exported before c2node_2 was stopped).

## 78. Test 22 (`replication_2node_1transmitter_2recv`) passes on `QSD5.279`; two product findings, both reproduced (2026-10-10)
Cluster 1 (sender, 2 nodes) = zfs1 + zfs2 at 10.11.11.200, cluster 2 (receiver, 1 node) = zfs3 at 10.11.11.100 (the test's "Cluster1"/"Cluster2" mapped to the container addresses). All 31 steps passed, no failed step; `buildrepl.sh 220` built both clusters in 33 min, the test itself took 87 min including the first-cluster build.
- **Finding 1: the admin password is the default again after a leader change.** Cluster 1's admin password (set with `hosts/config username=admin password=...`) was rejected after `stopnode.sh zfs1` (leader and pool owner) and the default `tmatem` worked again on the new leader zfs2; the receiving cluster then took the same (default) hash through the §64 pull, so both clusters ended on `tmatem`. Reproduces the open item of §77. Not yet analysed (the hash lives in `usershash/admin` of the old leader's etcd; the survivor's copy apparently never received the change, or `UnixChangePass` of the first-boot default overwrites it on promotion).
- **Finding 2: scheduled jobs are lost when a node that does not own the pool wins the race.** `putcron.sh` (leader only) files `call/<id>` with `/TopStor/Snapshotnowhost::<pool>/<vol>::...`; `croncall.py` runs on EVERY node (`croncalllooper.sh`, 9 s loop) and the node that deletes the key first runs it; `Snapshotnowhost` exits with "host not owner" on the node that does not hold the pool, so the snapshot (and its replication) of that tick is lost. Measured on the 2-minute schedule of step 27 after c1node_1 had returned: 4 ticks, 2 snapshots (08:38 and 08:40 UTC went to the non-owner). With one node alive every tick works (step 30). Proposed fix: `croncall.py` must not delete/run a `Snapshotnowhost` call whose pool is not imported on this node (leave the key for the owner), same for any `call` whose first argument is a pool name.
- **Result.** Test 22 passed; timings in `scripts/qc-harness/timings/test22.tsv`, steps in `scripts/qc-harness/tests/test22.*`.

## 79. Test 23 (`replication_single_node_clusters`) steps 1-22 pass on `QSD5.280`; the cross-cluster pool adoption is closed (2026-10-10)
Cluster 1 = zfs3 (10.11.11.100), cluster 2 = zfs1 (10.11.11.200), one node each, same host kernel. No step failed. Branch `QSD5.280` (from `QSD5.279`) carries three guards found while running it.
- **Open findings.** The admin password after a leader change (§78) is not analysed yet. The receiver's replicated volume showed `ipaddress None` right after the node restart (shown again with the IP a minute later in an earlier look; not reproduced).
- **Result.** Steps 1-22 pass (ids 656-679, 684 with the config zips of both clusters), 65 m 7 s (`timings/test23.tsv`, `tests/test23.*`).

## 80. Deleting a user did not delete his home folder, so the name could not be reused — `QSD5.281` (2026-10-10)
Found by the QualityCheck test `users_2nodes_OneCluster` (test 26, `QSD5.280`), step 13 "Add user usr12 with home folder (10.11.11.156), delete the user, try creating another user with same name" (`on_failure: stop`, test ended). Steps 1-12 passed on `QSD5.280`, including the take-over of the primary (portal back after 23 s, pool imported at the first attempt, all 10 share containers on the survivor within 2 minutes: the §66 fix holds).
- **Symptom.** `users/userdel name=usr12 tenant=Cluster` removed the user, but the HOME volume `usr12_<id>` (dataset, container `HOMEE-10.11.11.156`, `volumes/HOMEE/...` record) stayed for ever; creating `usr12` again answered `"adduser": "rejected: the name is already used by a user, a group or a volume"`. `cmdaudit.log` showed only `UnixDelUser` posted, never `VolumeDeleteHOME`.
- **Root cause (both flavours).** §54 (`QSD5.257`) made `userdel` in `fapi.py` look for the user's HOME volumes with `vol.get('prot') == 'HOME'`. `allphysicalinfo.py` takes `prot` from the second segment of the etcd key, and home volumes are written as `volumes/HOMEE/<host>/<pool>/<name>` (`VolumeCheck.py`), so `prot` is `HOMEE` and the condition never matched. It was never verified against a user created through the API of a node with that key naming.
- **Fix.** `TopStor/fapi.py`: `vol.get('prot') in ('HOME', 'HOMEE')`.
- **Proof (live, zfs2 leader, flask restarted with the new file).** `userdel usr12` -> 8 s later the HOME volume is gone from `volumes/HOME/volumesinfo`, `zfs list` has no `usr12_*` dataset and `HOMEE-10.11.11.156` is no longer in the node's docker; then `UnixAddUser usr12` with `10.11.11.156` again -> `"adduser": "accepted"` and a new `usr12_<id>` home on .156 (add / delete / add, same name, same ip).
- **Note.** Other users' homes of the test cluster were untouched; the guard for `admin`/`Everyone`/`NoUser` is unchanged.
- **Second change of the same branch.** `uservalid.py` `PASS_MIN` 3 -> 4 and `topstorweb/src/utils/userRules.js` `USER_PASS_MIN = 4`: test step 20/21 says a password of <= 3 characters must be refused, the product accepted exactly 3 (live: `shortp`/3 chars refused, `okfour`/4 accepted; same on the change-password path, `Hostconfig.py`).
- **Open at that time (re-run step 18).** two `UnixAddUser` of the same name sent about a second apart: both were accepted by the guard, only one user results (the later one is refused "a user with this name already exists"); step 17 (home folder without IP) creates nothing but gives no `adduser` rejection text.

## 81. Deleting a user deleted the passwords of every user whose name contains his — `QSD5.282` (2026-10-10)
Found in the local re-run of test 26 (`users_2nodes_OneCluster`, `QSD5.281`) at step 32 "login with usr12 and change its password to usradmin1" (`on_failure: stop`), after step 28 "delete usr1".
- **Symptom.** After `users/userdel name=usr1` the users `usr10`, `usr11`, `usr12`, `usr13` and `usr16` could no longer log in (`login` -> `"token": "baduser"`) although they were still in the user list and in `/etc/passwd`; `usr2`..`usr9` were fine. `etcdget usershash --prefix` had lost exactly the keys `usershash/usr10 .. usershash/usr16`.
- **Root cause (both flavours).** `UnixDelUser` ran `/pace/etcddel.py $etcd usershash $username`. In `etcddel.py` a second argument is not a key: every key/value pair under the prefix whose text merely *contains* the argument is deleted (`if x in str(y)`), so the name `usr1` matched `usr10`..`usr19`. The same pattern was in `UnixDelGroup` (`Grp1` would delete `Grp10`), `UnixDelUser_sync` and `UnixDelGroup_sync` (local etcd). A password hash removed from etcd is not recreated by the sync, so the users were locked out for good after a leader change.
- **Fix.** `TopStor/UnixDelUser`: `etcddel.py $etcd usershash/$username` (exact key); `UnixDelGroup`: `usersigroup/$username`; `UnixDelUser_sync`: `users /$username/` (the delimited form the main script already used); `UnixDelGroup_sync`: `usersigroup/$username`. `apply.d/QSD5.282` hooks are empty.
- **Proof (live, zfs1 leader after the take-over).** Users `ut1` and `ut10` created; hashes of `usr10..usr16`, `ut1`, `ut10` listed; `userdel ut1` -> after 25 s the list is the same without `ut1` only; `ut10` and `usr12` log in with their passwords. Then `usr12` logged in and changed its password to `usradmin1` (new password accepted, old one refused).
- **Note.** The damaged users of this cluster were repaired by setting their passwords again (`user/changepass`). A name that is a prefix of another is a normal case (usr1/usr10, Grp1/Grp10), so this would have hit every customer deleting such a user.

## 82. A password changed on the leader was lost after a fail over — `QSD5.283` (2026-10-10)
Found in the local re-run of test 26 (`QSD5.282`), steps 30-35: after "admin changes the password to Admin2" (30) and "usr12 changes its password to usradmin1" (32) the sudden death of the leader (34) left the cluster on the **old** passwords (`admin/Admin2` -> `baduser`, `usr12/usradmin1` -> `baduser`). This is the finding left open in §63/§78 ("admin password reverts after leader change"), now with the cause.
- **Root cause (both flavours).** `Hostconfig.py` stores the new hash only in the **leader's** etcd and queues `sync/passwd/UnixChangePass_<user>_<req>/request`. A follower handles it in `checksyncs.syncrequest` (branch `special1`) by running `/TopStor/UnixChangePass`, and that script reads the hash from the node's **own** etcd (`etcdgetlocal.py usershash/<user>`). Nothing had copied the leader's key there (the `broadcasttolocal` call in `Hostconfig.py` is commented out; `usersyncall` hands a hash to `UnixAddUser` only for users that have `usersinfo`, never for admin). So the follower re-applied the old hash to `/etc/passwd`, and when it became the leader the old hash was the cluster's password again. A key that was missing locally (a user whose hash had been deleted, §81) stayed missing.
- **Fix.** `pace/checksyncs.py` `syncrequest`, branch `special1`: on a node that is not the leader the new `usershash/<user>` is read from the leader and put into the node's own etcd before `UnixChangePass` runs. `pace/usersyncall.py` `usersyncall` (initial/periodic user sync of a follower): the leader's `usershash/admin` is copied into the local etcd and applied with `UnixChangePass admin admin` when it differs, because admin has no `usersinfo`. `apply.d/QSD5.283` hooks empty.
- **Proof (live, zfs2 leader, zfs1 follower on `QSD5.283`).** `user/changepass usr13` (leader) -> after 10 s `etcdgetlocal usershash/usr13` on zfs1 equals the leader's value (before: the old hash for ever); `admin` changed to a new password -> the follower's hash equal after the join; zfs2 stopped with `stopnode.sh` -> zfs1 leader after 41 s, `admin/<new>` and `usr13/<new>` log in, the old `usr13` password is refused.
- **Observation, not changed.** After a take-over `admin/tmatem` (the password the cluster was created with, `usershashadm/admin`) still logs in next to the new admin password; that is `UnixChkUser`'s admin fallback.
- **Local re-run of test 26** (38 steps) is now complete on `QSD5.282`/`QSD5.283`: steps 24-38 pass; step 28 found §81, step 32/35 found this section.

## 83. A pool create right after a destroy failed with `Device or resource busy` and made no pool — `QSD5.284` (2026-10-10)
Found by the QualityCheck test `diskgroups_2nodes` (test 10, `QSD5.283`), step 14 "Create RAID 50 using 10x10GB Disks" (`on_failure: stop`, test ended). Second occurrence of the transient mentioned at the end of §67.
- **Symptom.** `POST pools/newpool redundancy=raid50 useable=64.2` answered HTTP 200 about 25 s after the previous pool had been deleted on the same disks; no pool appeared for 3 minutes (`zpool list` empty, API without pool, disks free). `/root/tmp2` showed the request reached `DGsetPool` as `raid50 <9 disks>` (the §67 fix holds); `/root/dgcreateerror` = `cannot open '/dev/disk/by-id/scsi-...-part1': Device or resource busy`.
- **Root cause (both flavours).** `DGsetPool` ran `zpool create` once. `zpool create -f` repartitions the disks and opens the new `-part1` a moment later; for a second or two udev/blkid still holds the new partition, and the single attempt ended the whole create (a pool-less `DGfa` message is all the user sees). A physical server has the same race, only less often (udev settles faster).
- **Fix.** `TopStor/DGsetPool`: function `zpoolcreate` (all ten `zpool create` calls), retries up to 8 times with `udevadm settle` + 5 s only when the error text contains `resource busy`; any other error is returned at once as before. Each retry is logged in `/root/dgcreateretry`.
- **Proof (live, node_1 owner).** Four cycles create RAID50 / wait ONLINE / delpool / waitnopool / create at once: all four pools created, cycle 2 hit the busy error and `/root/dgcreateretry` shows one retry, the pool came ONLINE 5 s later; the other cycles needed none.
- **Local re-run** of test 10 follows on this branch.

## 84. RAID50 / RAID60 could never be "Highly Available, balanced" on two nodes — `QSD5.285` (2026-10-10)
Found in the local re-run of test 10 (`diskgroups_2nodes`, `QSD5.284`), step 15 "Wait till the new pool is highly available - Balanced" (RAID50, 10 x 10 GB disks over node_1 and node_2).
- **Symptom.** The RAID50 pool stayed "Highly Available, not balanced" for 5 minutes and forever. `zpool status` showed three `raidz1` groups of 3 disks, each 2 disks of one node + 1 of the other.
- **Root cause (both flavours).** `raidrank.py` calls a vdev balanced only when it has the same number of disks of every node; a 3-disk group (RAID50) can never be split equally over 2 nodes, a 4-disk group (RAID60) can. The width 3/4 was hard-coded in `raid5060.py`, `fapi.py` and four loops of `DGsetPool`.
- **Fix.** `TopStor/raid5060.py`: `raidwidth(base, nhosts)` = smallest width >= base divisible by the number of nodes (RAID50: 3 -> 4 on 2 nodes, stays 3 on 3 nodes; RAID60 stays 4 on 2 nodes), used by `getraid50/60` (disk counts and useable sizes offered) and `selectraid50/60`; `interleave()` orders the chosen disks so every consecutive group has the same number per node. `fapi.py` sends the width in the command word (`raid50w4`, `addraid60w4` ...); `DGsetPool` strips the `w<N>` into `RW` and uses `${RW:-3}` / `${RW:-4}` in the group loops and checks. A plain `raid50`/`raid60` (older callers) behaves as before.
- **Consequence for the UI.** With 2 nodes RAID50 is offered in groups of 4 (8, 12 ... disks, useable `size*3*groups`): 10 x 1 GB class gives 6.42 for 8 disks.
- **Proof (live, 2 nodes).** `newpool raid50 6.42` -> two `raidz1` groups of 4, each 2 disks of node_1 + 2 of node_2, `ONLINE`, availability text "Highly Available, balanced".
